issues.detail: Error handling is limited to a failedRequestHandler log line, with no guidance on CAPTCHA or block detection, session retirement, timeouts, or empty or changed selectors.
The two examples are prose descriptions of the agent's actions with no concrete code or output, and Example 2 (price monitoring) omits the named dataset, comparison and alerting code.

scenarios.name: books-router-csv-export
scenarios.rationale: A uses CheerioCrawler with createCheerioRouter, separate LISTING and DETAIL handlers, enqueueLinks for the next page, pushData, Dataset exportToCSV, and both maxRequestsPerMinute and respectRobotsTxtFile, though maxRequestsPerCrawl is only mentioned in a note; B uses CheerioCrawler but has no router (a single if/else handler), no politeness or robots options, and a manual CSV writer instead of exportToCSV, and its stale-data note contradicts itself.

scenarios.name: js-rendered-infinite-scroll-shop
scenarios.rationale: B hits nearly every rubric item: PlaywrightCrawler, waitForSelector, the built-in infiniteScroll helper, pushData, and a lowered maxConcurrency (5) with a note that browsers are heavy. A uses PlaywrightCrawler and waitForSelector but scrolls by hand, leans on waitForTimeout and networkidle, doesn't use infiniteScroll, and only mentions maxConcurrency in passing without setting it.

scenarios.name: daily-price-monitor-named-dataset
scenarios.rationale: Both explain the default-storage purge and use a named store with diffing, but both use a named KeyValueStore rather than a named Dataset. B does use pushData into a named Dataset (price-history), uses PlaywrightCrawler, and explicitly warns against the default dataset. A uses CheerioCrawler and mentions the Playwright swap, but never uses pushData or a dataset.
